segments.title: Li Luo's Fried Noodles
segments.content:
Chapter 11 Li Luo's Fried Noodles

Sitting in front of the computer in Ying Chanxi's study, Li Luo's expression was a bit helpless.

When he had planned to try his hand at his old profession, he hadn't thought of this complication, forgetting that a minor needed a guardian's consent to sign a contract.

Although Li Luo had been going to the shop to help out every morning since the high school entrance exams ended, greatly improving his rebellious image in his parents' eyes.

But considering the short time since this change, Li Luo wasn't in a hurry to tell them about his attempt at writing web novels.

After all, the results of the high school entrance exam were coming out tomorrow morning.

Li Luo felt that the chances of getting their consent would be much higher after his parents saw his report card.

As for why he chose to write an urban entertainment novel... it was naturally because that was the only genre he had ever written in his past life.

Li Luo had considered directly using his memory palace to find a wildly popular web novel and copying it to make a fortune.

But after giving it a try, Li Luo knew he had been too careless.

As everyone knows, when reading web novels, you basically skim ten lines at a glance.

Sometimes, just by looking at the chapter title, you know what the author is padding it with and just skip it entirely.

This led to... Li Luo trying to recall those wildly popular works he had read, and he realized that expending the mental energy to remember them would be an exercise in futility.

For the memory palace, the deeper the impression Li Luo had of something and the more carefully he had read it, the less mental energy it would take to recall.

But novels in the male-oriented category often ran for millions of words, and he had devoured them by skimming ten lines at a time. Even if he only recalled a few thousand words a day, Li Luo's brain would crash as if it were about to explode.

But the good news was, Li Luo's own skill level was decent.

Although he couldn't replicate them word for word, as a former industry insider, Li Luo still had a firm grasp on many key plots and trope designs.

Especially now, in 2014, there weren't many outstanding works in the urban entertainment genre.

The ones that could achieve success were either set against the backdrop of the Chinese entertainment industry or the currently trending Korean entertainment industry.

Entertainment novels set in a fictional, parallel world had not yet shown many signs of appearing.

Within the urban genre, the most popular types at the moment were still urban fantasy, or similar cool-man novels like a king of soldiers coming down from the mountains or a miracle-working traditional Chinese doctor, as well as those officialdom novels.

But Li Luo remembered very clearly that in the second half of this year, a divine entertainment novel was about to burst onto the scene and would, in the following years, become a sensation across the entire web.

So Li Luo didn't think about it any further and typed his novel's title onto the computer screen—I'm Really Not a Star.

He had no thoughts of making a huge fortune.

As long as he could get a little more pocket money each month in high school, his life would be quite comfortable.

With this simple thought in mind, Li Luo smoothly received contract offers from several editors, and one editor even proactively added him as a QQ friend.

Qian Zhou: So... what is your current age?

Far away in Changning City, Qian Zhou stared at his computer screen, wearing the expression of an old man looking at a smartphone, highly suspecting that this guy on the other end was trying to pull a fast one on him.

Chong Ran: I'm 15 this year. I'll be 16 after my birthday in the latter half of the year.

Qian Zhou: Are you sure you're not kidding?

Chong Ran: Absolutely, editor. Just give me a few more days, I should be able to convince my mom.

Qian Zhou: Have you written novels before?

Chong Ran: No.

Qian Zhou: Then this opening, did you write it yourself?

Chong Ran: I wrote it myself.

Looking at the chat history on QQ, Qian Zhou fell into deep thought for a moment.

The plot, content, and pacing of "I'm Really Not a Star" swirled in his mind.

Finally, he thought, could it be that in this world, such a thing as a prodigious talent really exists?

A 15-year-old kid could actually write about the protagonist's worldly wisdom and way of doing things?

He would have believed it if you told him it was written by a greasy 35-year-old middle-aged man!

Qian Zhou: If that's really the case, then you should have a good talk with your mother.

Qian Zhou: In any case, whether she agrees or not, let me know.

Qian Zhou: If your mother has any questions, she can come to me as well.

Chong Ran: Okay, thank you, editor.

After dealing with the editor, Li Luo continued to tap on the keyboard.

His memory palace operated at high speed, providing him with all sorts of material and plot devices, and the novel's content poured out like flowing water.

After returning home in the evening and having a few bites of dinner, he immediately went back to the study in Ying Chanxi's house to continue his work.

It wasn't until around eight-thirty at night.

The sound of the front door opening was heard.

Ying Chanxi, carrying her school bag and wearing slippers, came from the entrance to the study and saw Li Luo engrossed in watching anime.

"Don't tell me you spent the whole day playing on the computer at my house again?" Ying Chanxi put her school bag on the sofa, then walked into the study and said with a helpless look, "You finally became willing to study. It's best to take advantage of the summer break and preview the high school textbooks."

Li Luo pressed the pause button, turned his head to look at Ying Chanxi who had just returned from the advanced summer class at No. 1 Affiliated High, and chuckled, "My dear Miss Ying Chanxi, may I ask, what is the purpose of the state-mandated summer vacation?"

"Uhm..." Ying Chanxi was stumped. She hesitated for a long time before finally saying, "To give students a break to rest?"

"That's right." Li Luo snapped his fingers, stood up from the chair, and pushed Ying Chanxi's shoulders to sit on the living room sofa.

He then walked behind the sofa and began to massage Ying Chanxi's shoulders, saying as he kneaded, "As they say, balance work and rest. After the arduous struggle of the last semester of junior high, the summer vacation is precisely the time for students to relax properly."

"How's the pressure?"

"Harder or lighter?"

"Mmm..." Ying Chanxi closed her eyes, enjoying Li Luo's service for a moment, "It's just right, but..."

Just as Ying Chanxi was about to refute Li Luo, her stomach was the first to let out a gurgling sound.

Li Luo raised an eyebrow and immediately started to laugh, "See? This is what happens when you don't relax and rest properly. You've studied your stomach into hunger."

Ying Chanxi's face flushed red. She covered her stomach and said with a straight face, "I'm not hungry."

"Want some fried noodles?" Li Luo stopped his hands, walked into the kitchen to check the ingredients in the fridge, and then asked.

"It's so late, it's not good to trouble your father again." Ying Chanxi quickly shook her head, "I'll just have a slice of bread to tide me over."

"Are you questioning my culinary skills?" Li Luo took some ingredients out of the fridge and winked at Ying Chanxi, "Just for some fried noodles, do you really think my dad needs to step in?"

"You're making it yourself?" Ying Chanxi's eyes widened slightly in surprise, "Can you do it?"

"You are challenging a man's bottom line." Li Luo gave a cold laugh and slammed the fridge door shut, "Wait in the living room."

After speaking, he pulled the kitchen's sliding door shut.

Ying Chanxi blinked, still not quite processing it.

But in a short while, the crisp sound of a kitchen knife chopping on a cutting board came from the kitchen.

Then, the enticing sound of fried noodles being stir-fried in a wok sizzled.

In less than ten minutes, two bowls of hot, fragrant fried noodles were brought out from the kitchen by Li Luo.

Ying Chanxi sat down at the dining table, looking at the bowl of steaming, fragrant fried noodles in front of her, momentarily speechless.

"Eat up." Li Luo handed her the chopsticks and sat opposite her. Without being polite, he dug in with a big mouthful, his words muffled as he ate, "Try my cooking. It's definitely no worse than my dad's."

"Okay." Ying Chanxi picked up her chopsticks, subconsciously raised her head and glanced at Li Luo, then turned her head to look around.

There was no one else in the spacious living room. Her father's bedroom had been dark for over half a month.

The light in the study was on because of Li Luo, and the kitchen light was still on too.

No family was by her side, but...

Feeling a mix of loss and reassurance, Ying Chanxi's gaze returned to Li Luo. Then, she lowered her head and took a small bite of the fried noodles.

It was really delicious.

"It's even more delicious than what Uncle makes," Ying Chanxi said, her feet resting on the rung of the chair as she enjoyed the delicious late-night snack in a well-behaved and quiet manner, praising Li Luo in a low voice.

"You've got some good taste," Li Luo said with a smug chuckle, then reminded her in a hushed tone, "But don't tell my dad that, okay?"

"Haha~" She was amused by him, "Are you afraid Uncle will be unconvinced if he finds out?"

"I'm afraid his Dao heart might shatter if he finds out his skills are inferior to his son's."

"Give you an inch and you'll take a mile." Ying Chanxi shot him a look, "But when did you learn to make fried noodles? I've never seen you cook before."

"There's a lot you haven't seen." Li Luo ate quickly and had already polished off his bowl. He stood up and stretched, "I cook, you wash the dishes, okay? I'm going to play on the computer."

"Got it." Ying Chanxi nodded in agreement, then reminded him, "You can only play until ten o'clock, okay?"

"OK OK."

After finishing the fried noodles, Ying Chanxi stood up to clear the bowls and plates, washed them in the kitchen, and then took a shower.

Originally, she had planned to study for a while after her shower, but Ying Chanxi thought about what Li Luo had said earlier. After some hesitation, she temporarily set aside the idea and walked into the study instead.

She moved a stool to sit next to Li Luo. Ying Chanxi looked at the anime playing on the computer screen and then asked, "The high school entrance exam results can be checked tomorrow, the 28th, at ten in the morning. Aren't you nervous?"

"Nervous about what?" Li Luo asked back, "Just wait for me at No. 1 Affiliated High."

Seeing him so certain even at the last minute, Ying Chanxi became even more suspicious, "Don't tell me you started asking Zhao Rongjun to help you review a long time ago? Are you really confident you can get into No. 1 Affiliated High?"

"Why would I lie to you?"

Hearing Li Luo still say this at this critical juncture, Ying Chanxi, who originally held no expectations for him, felt her heart inexplicably start to beat faster.

Could it be... that in high school, there was still a chance for her and Li Luo to be in the same school?

At this thought, Ying Chanxi instantly grew nervous, a faint sense of anticipation for tomorrow's exam results building up.

"How about we play a game?" Li Luo closed the anime, opened a web browser, and searched for 4399 mini-games, "Fireboy and Watergirl, still know how to play?"

"You're underestimating me a little." Ying Chanxi shifted her stool, moving closer to Li Luo until their arms were touching, "I just don't usually play, it's not that I don't know how."

"Why aren't you studying anymore today? You even came to play on the computer with me."

"Didn't a certain someone say we need to balance work and rest, and can relax a bit?"

"As expected of Yucai's number one academic god, you learn so fast."

The two of them bickered as they quickly got into the game.

But halfway through, Ying Chanxi's hand trembled several times, and the Watergirl she was controlling evaporated directly in a sea of lava.

"Are you even any good?" Li Luo looked at her with a dubious expression.

"Don't be noisy." Ying Chanxi puffed out her cheeks, "It's all your fault for saying you could get into No. 1 Affiliated High. Now my head is full of your exam results, I'm so nervous."

"My results, what are you nervous about?"

"If you get in, we'll be in the same school again." Ying Chanxi's eyes widened as she looked at Li Luo, speaking in all seriousness, "If you work a little harder in high school, maybe you could get into Qianjiang University with me?"

"You think quite highly of me." Li Luo couldn't help but laugh, "Qianjiang University? Even for students at No. 1 Affiliated High, only the top fifty in the entire school each year have a chance to even touch the threshold, right?"

"One must have dreams." Ying Chanxi's eyes sparkled as she stared at Li Luo and said, "If you can really get into No. 1 Affiliated High, I don't think Qianjiang University is a problem either."

"I feel like you have more confidence in me than I do."
